message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is simply called a **multinucleated cell**.  
In biology we often refer to such a structure as a **syncytium** (literally “many nuclei”), especially when the nuclei are spread throughout a continuous cytoplasm.

**Examples of multinucleated cells**

| Cell type | Typical function | Where you find it |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Skeletal muscle fiber (myocyte)** | Contraction of muscle | Skeletal muscle tissue |
| **Osteoclast** | Bone resorption | Bone remodeling |
| **Syncytiotrophoblast** | Nutrient transfer in placenta | Placental villi |
| **Multinucleated giant cells** | Inflammatory response, foreign body reaction | Granulomas, chronic inflammation |
| **Myoblast fusion product** | Early muscle development | Developing muscle tissue |

So if you’re looking for a generic term, “multinucleated cell” or “syncytium” is the right answer. If you need a specific example, skeletal muscle fibers are the most familiar.
